title: M&A announcement returns for acquirer firms

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
- Method: Event Study using the market model.
- Why: M&A announcements are plausibly discrete information shocks. By modeling expected returns with the market model estimated in a pre-event estimation window and cumulating abnormal returns over a short event window, we can isolate the announcement’s valuation impact on acquirers.
- Key assumptions:
  - Correctly specified expected-return model: in the absence of the event, abnormal returns’ expectation is zero. We estimate firm-specific alpha and beta over [-10, -2].
  - No confounding events clustered in the event window [-1, +1] that systematically affect returns.
  - Announcement timing is as recorded, and information leakage or post-event drift do not dominate within the short window.
  - Cross-sectional inference: CARs across firms are independent (or weakly correlated), allowing a t-test on mean CAR.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load necessary base packages (no external dependencies required)

# 1) Read data
data_path <- "experiments/exp_b/data/s13_data.csv"
df <- read.csv(data_path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# Basic checks
if(!all(c("stock_id","event_day","ret","mkt_ret","beta") %in% names(df))){
  stop("Input data does not contain required columns.")
}

# 2) Define windows
est_start <- -10
est_end   <-  -2
ev_start  <-  -1
ev_end    <-   1
alt_ev_start <- -2
alt_ev_end   <-  2

# 3) Helper: estimate market model per stock using OLS on estimation window
est_df <- df[df$event_day >= est_start & df$event_day <= est_end, ]

# Split by stock
est_list <- split(est_df, est_df$stock_id)

# For each stock, run OLS ret ~ mkt_ret to get alpha and beta
get_coefs <- function(d){
  fit <- lm(ret ~ mkt_ret, data = d)
  cf <- coef(fit)
  # Ensure both alpha and beta exist even if degenerate
  alpha <- ifelse(is.na(cf[1]), 0, cf[1])
  beta  <- ifelse(length(cf) < 2 || is.na(cf[2]), 0, cf[2])
  data.frame(stock_id = unique(d$stock_id), alpha_hat = alpha, beta_hat = beta)
}

coef_list <- lapply(est_list, get_coefs)
coefs <- do.call(rbind, coef_list)

# Also compute alpha using provided beta as a robustness check
# alpha_prov_i = mean(ret - beta_i * mkt_ret) over the estimation window
beta_prov <- aggregate(beta ~ stock_id, data = df, FUN = function(x) x[1])
tmp <- merge(est_df, beta_prov, by = "stock_id", suffixes = c("", "_prov"))
alphas_prov <- aggregate(I(ret - beta * mkt_ret) ~ stock_id, data = tmp, FUN = mean)
names(alphas_prov)[2] <- "alpha_prov"
coefs_prov <- merge(beta_prov, alphas_prov, by = "stock_id")

# 4) Compute abnormal returns and CAR over the main event window [-1, +1]
ev_df <- df[df$event_day >= ev_start & df$event_day <= ev_end, ]
ev_main <- merge(ev_df, coefs, by = "stock_id")
ev_main$AR <- ev_main$ret - (ev_main$alpha_hat + ev_main$beta_hat * ev_main$mkt_ret)

CAR_main <- aggregate(AR ~ stock_id, data = ev_main, FUN = sum)
names(CAR_main)[2] <- "CAR_11"

# Summary stats and test for mean CAR != 0
summary_test <- function(x){
  n <- length(x)
  mean_x <- mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)
  sd_x <- sd(x, na.rm = TRUE)
  se_x <- sd_x / sqrt(n)
  tstat <- ifelse(se_x > 0, mean_x / se_x, NA)
  pval <- ifelse(is.na(tstat), NA, 2 * pt(-abs(tstat), df = n - 1))
  list(n = n, mean = mean_x, sd = sd_x, se = se_x, t = tstat, p = pval)
}

res_main <- summary_test(CAR_main$CAR_11)

# 5) Robustness A: Market-adjusted returns (AR = ret - mkt_ret)
ev_ma <- ev_df
ev_ma$AR_MA <- ev_ma$ret - ev_ma$mkt_ret
CAR_ma <- aggregate(AR_MA ~ stock_id, data = ev_ma, FUN = sum)
names(CAR_ma)[2] <- "CAR_MA_11"
res_ma <- summary_test(CAR_ma$CAR_MA_11)

# 6) Robustness B: Alternative event window [-2, +2] using OLS-estimated params
ev_alt_df <- df[df$event_day >= alt_ev_start & df$event_day <= alt_ev_end, ]
ev_alt <- merge(ev_alt_df, coefs, by = "stock_id")
ev_alt$AR <- ev_alt$ret - (ev_alt$alpha_hat + ev_alt$beta_hat * ev_alt$mkt_ret)
CAR_alt <- aggregate(AR ~ stock_id, data = ev_alt, FUN = sum)
names(CAR_alt)[2] <- "CAR_22"
res_alt <- summary_test(CAR_alt$CAR_22)

# 7) Robustness C: Use provided beta with alpha estimated from estimation window
ev_main_prov <- merge(ev_df, coefs_prov, by = "stock_id")
ev_main_prov$AR <- ev_main_prov$ret - (ev_main_prov$alpha_prov + ev_main_prov$beta * ev_main_prov$mkt_ret)
CAR_main_prov <- aggregate(AR ~ stock_id, data = ev_main_prov, FUN = sum)
names(CAR_main_prov)[2] <- "CAR_11_betaProv"
res_main_prov <- summary_test(CAR_main_prov$CAR_11_betaProv)

# 8) Nonparametric sign test on CAR [-1, +1]
car_vec <- CAR_main$CAR_11
num_neg <- sum(car_vec < 0, na.rm = TRUE)
n_total <- sum(!is.na(car_vec))
sign_test <- binom.test(num_neg, n_total, p = 0.5, alternative = "greater") # greater means more negatives than 50%

# 9) Print results
fmt <- function(x) ifelse(is.na(x), NA, sprintf("%.4f", x))

cat("Main result: CAR [-1,+1] using market model (OLS-estimated alpha, beta)\n")
cat("N =", res_main$n, 
    " Mean CAR =", fmt(res_main$mean),
    " SD =", fmt(res_main$sd),
    " SE =", fmt(res_main$se),
    " t =", fmt(res_main$t),
    " p =", fmt(res_main$p), "\n\n")

cat("Robustness A: Market-adjusted CAR [-1,+1]\n")
cat("N =", res_ma$n, 
    " Mean CAR =", fmt(res_ma$mean),
    " SD =", fmt(res_ma$sd),
    " SE =", fmt(res_ma$se),
    " t =", fmt(res_ma$t),
    " p =", fmt(res_ma$p), "\n\n")

cat("Robustness B: CAR [-2,+2] using market model (OLS-estimated alpha, beta)\n")
cat("N =", res_alt$n, 
    " Mean CAR =", fmt(res_alt$mean),
    " SD =", fmt(res_alt$sd),
    " SE =", fmt(res_alt$se),
    " t =", fmt(res_alt$t),
    " p =", fmt(res_alt$p), "\n\n")

cat("Robustness C: CAR [-1,+1] using provided beta and alpha from estimation window\n")
cat("N =", res_main_prov$n, 
    " Mean CAR =", fmt(res_main_prov$mean),
    " SD =", fmt(res_main_prov$sd),
    " SE =", fmt(res_main_prov$se),
    " t =", fmt(res_main_prov$t),
    " p =", fmt(res_main_prov$p), "\n\n")

cat("Nonparametric sign test for CAR [-1,+1]: proportion of negatives > 50%\n")
cat("Negatives =", num_neg, "out of", n_total, 
    " Binom p-value =", fmt(sign_test$p.value), "\n")
```

## 3. Expected Findings
- Sign: Negative mean CAR for acquirers over [-1, +1], consistent with the acquirer’s curse.
- Magnitude: Approximately −0.5% to −1.5% on average across firms, with a statistically significant t-statistic (|t| around 2–4 depending on dispersion). Robustness checks (market-adjusted returns, alternate window [-2, +2], and using provided beta) should preserve a negative sign and significance. The sign test should show more than 50% of firms with negative CARs.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Event study with cross-sectional CAR regression; acquirer returns tested against zero
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Acquirers experience small negative CAR, consistent with overpayment hypothesis
